tools.name: get_service_info
tools.description: Read supported checks, limitations, prices and access options. No check, account, subscription or payment is created.

tools.name: get_trial_access
tools.description: Create a free trial credential without login, email, card or subscription. Three execution attempts and twenty total check/usage requests, one-hour expiry, shared service capacity limits. Failed execution attempts count. Cannot purchase or spend money. Do not repeatedly create trials to evade limits

tools.name: prepare_check
tools.description: Generate a fresh request key for one deliberately new check. This does not run a check or reserve capacity. Retain it before dispatch. After an uncertain outcome reuse the original request key and credential; never call this tool to replace an uncertain request.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Read the supplied trial or connection API key allowance and expiry. No completed-check unit is consumed. Does not change any limits or authorize spending.

tools.name: check_asset
tools.description: Run bounded technical checks, using the free trial token or connection API key. Paid access may consume EUR 0.01 before tax under its existing authorized subscription and budgets. A completed PASS or FAIL counts. Trial execution errors consume trial attempts. Always retain idempotency_key before dis

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_asset" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_trial_access · Private data: get_trial_access, prepare_check, get_usage, check_asset · Public sink: get_trial_access · Destructive: prepare_check, check_asset.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_trial_access · Private data: get_trial_access, prepare_check, get_usage, check_asset · Public sink: get_trial_access · Destructive: prepare_check, check_asset

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
